page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-16 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Simultaneous multithreading is enabled, providing two threads per core. The machine is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, reflecting an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle discrete GPUs or local disk storage, necessitating remote persistent disks for data storage. Processor instruction support includes AVX-512 variants such as AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16, along with cryptographic features including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark testing shows strong single-core CPU execution, marked by an upper-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2865.18 and a strong Geekbench text processing result of 2497.0. Overall multi-core compute metrics place in the middle 50%, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10058.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 24415.71. A primary architectural tradeoff lies in uncached memory bandwidth: while cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaches 1132.34 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB reads register at 37.8 GB/sec and uncached writes fall into the bottom decile at 12.91 GB/sec.

The 1:8 core-to-memory configuration delivers high resource density for workloads constrained by RAM rather than raw parallel compute. The instance is technically suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, text processing pipelines, Clang compilation jobs, and general enterprise application hosting. Workloads reliant on sustained high-throughput uncached memory writes or dense matrix GPU acceleration are not aligned with this hardware profile.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-16 is a memory-dense virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPUs, depending entirely on network-attached storage for non-volatile data. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, characterized by high Geekbench text processing and stress-ng single-thread scores. However, uncached memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained, particularly during large-block write operations. Because of its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suited for memory-bound applications, including Redis caching layers, medium databases, software compilation, and text processing workloads.
